title: Beam with two loaded overhangs: moment in the middle portion and midspan deflection

source.work: ANSYS, Inc., Mechanical APDL Verification Manual (public help site ansyshelp.ansys.com)
source.notes: problem statement taken from the vendor page (text; the sketch was not readable). The page cites: Timoshenko, Strength of Materials, Part I, 3rd ed. 1955, p. 98, problem 4 - NOT opened for this project; no number is taken from it. The page's 'Target' values are recorded as printed; the program's own results are not used.

analysis: Plane problem in the global X-Y plane (Y vertical); the out-of-plane DOFs (uz, rx, ry) of every node are held; in-plane bending about local z. Beam of 480 in on two supports 240 in apart, with two overhangs of 120 in; 10,000 lb/ft downward on both overhangs only; A = 50.65 in^2, Iz = 7892 in^4, depth 30 in, E = 30e6 psi. First-order analysis without shear deformation. The page prints the bending stress in the middle portion (compression at the bottom); the target here is the bending moment = stress x Iz / (depth / 2) = stress x 526.1333 in^3. Reference values: computed here from this statement (verification/derive/vendor_reference.py); the textbook cited by the vendor page was not opened and no number is taken from it.
